message.content: **Order filled: bought 44 shares of AAPL at $222.75 (≈$9,801), within the mandate.** AAPL was quoted at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), so my limit sat right at the ask — effectively at market — and the fill came at $222.75. The position ($9,801) is under the $10,000 per-order cap and the only trade today, so total spend is well inside the $20,000 daily limit; it was a buy of a permitted name (AAPL) funded entirely from the $50,000 cash balance, with no withdrawals. **Why I bought:** Apple's fiscal 2024 results, reported October 31 and filed on Form 10-K November 1, showed continuing growth and profitability — quarterly revenue of $94.9B, up 6% year over year, and full-year revenue of **$391.0B**, net income of **$93.7B**, and diluted EPS of **$6.08** (the earnings figure absorbed a one-time $10.2B tax charge, so underlying profitability was stronger still). Growth in the flagship September quarter plus the Apple Intelligence / iPhone 16 rollout give a positive catalyst path, and the stock was trading quietly rather than on a post-earnings spike, letting me enter near the market. I did encounter one unreliable mirror site quoting FY2024 revenue of $361.2B and EPS of $5.12; I discarded those numbers after cross-checking the newsroom release and the trusted filing lookup, which agree exactly ($391,035M, $93,736M, $6.08/share).
